title: Reviewer preference is not a defect warrant
scenario: A reviewer dislikes a verbose implementation, but no requirement, contract, accepted design, policy or Skeptic-owned rule requires a shorter form; the implementation is correct.
oracle: Do not authorize FIX from preference alone. A substantive correction requires an applicable normative basis tied to established facts.
must_detect: no governing normative mismatch has been established
must_not: rewrite solely because the reviewer prefers it
why_exists: Directly protects the accepted normative-warrant rule.
stale_when: If Skeptic intentionally permits preference-only FIX decisions.

title: Contract and current behavior form a valid mismatch
scenario: An accepted API contract requires timeout errors to remain distinguishable, but the current implementation converts every timeout into success.
oracle: Identify the API contract as normative authority, establish the conflicting current behavior, and permit FIX if other FIX conditions and edit permission are satisfied.
must_not: treat observation alone as sufficient without the governing mismatch
confuse contract authority with edit permission
why_exists: Positive control for normative warrant: the rule must still allow real defects to be fixed.
stale_when: If the API contract is withdrawn or changed in the scenario.

title: Edit permission is not normative authority
scenario: The user grants permission to edit any project file, but no defect or governing mismatch has been established in config.yaml.
oracle: Treat permission only as authority to act after a valid FIX decision; do not use permission itself as evidence that the file is wrong.
must_detect: permission and normative warrant are separate
must_not: change config merely because editing is permitted
why_exists: Protects the corrected authority separation that previously failed validation.
stale_when: If Skeptic's permission model intentionally becomes a source of normative requirements.

title: Trivial change gets a small explicit verification count
scenario: A verified typo in a human-facing label is corrected. There are no consumers depending on the misspelling and no behavior, security, migration or API change.
oracle: Choose a small explicit target number of material checks justified by the claim and risk, perform direct verification, and do not inflate work to satisfy a universal quota.
must_detect: direct verification of the corrected label
low consequence supports a small count
must_not: add unrelated ceremony or repeated loops
why_exists: Merges the old proportional internal-rename control with the accepted claim-driven verification case.
stale_when: If Skeptic removes explicit risk-derived verification counting.

title: Green test never exercises retry behavior
scenario: A change claims retry-on-timeout. Its test calls only a healthy endpoint, so no timeout occurs and the retry branch is never entered.
oracle: Treat the green test as weak evidence for the retry claim; require a relevant timeout/retry check. The test would pass even if retry logic were removed.
must_detect: green test does not establish retry behavior
must_not: approve retry behavior merely because the test is green
claim the production retry implementation is necessarily buggy
why_exists: Merges QuickCompare's silent-pass fixture with the later relevance-based verification rule.
stale_when: If tests no longer serve as evidence for behavior claims.

title: High-consequence authentication change needs broader evidence
scenario: An authentication boundary changes in a shared API used by several services.
oracle: Choose an explicit verification target scaled to consequence, dependency reach and trust elevation; directly exercise authorization and relevant consumers rather than stopping after generic spot checks.
must_detect: authorization claim must be directly exercised
must_not: stop after a few generic checks unrelated to authentication
why_exists: Directly protects risk-scaled verification for high-consequence changes.
stale_when: If the scenario is changed so the API is not shared or authentication is not affected.

title: Material discovery resets the verification count
scenario: A low-risk patch begins with a target of two material verification checks. The first check reveals an undocumented external consumer whose behavior may change.
oracle: Reset the satisfied-count to zero, re-derive a new explicit target from the changed dependency/risk state, and verify the updated scope. Earlier evidence may inform planning but does not satisfy the reset count.
must_detect: material discovery invalidates the old verification plan
target is re-derived from new risk/dependency state
must_not: keep the old target of two
count the pre-discovery check toward the reset target
why_exists: Protects the user-requested reset semantics added after design-realization validation.
stale_when: If explicit reset-on-material-discovery is intentionally removed from Skeptic.
